concepts.name: Election Commission of India: scope, composition, functions, machinery and removal
concepts.description: Article 324 body, its composition and tenure, administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial functions, assisting officers and the removal of the CEC and other Commissioners.
concepts.idea: The ECI is a permanent constitutional body whose members are appointed by the President, whose CEC alone has judge-like removal protection, and which runs central elections through a pyramid of officers.
concepts.rule: The ECI is a permanent independent body under Article 324 superintending elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President; Panchayat and Municipal polls belong to State Election Commissions. It consists of the CEC and as many other Commissioners as the President fixes, with the CEC as chairman; they hold office for six years or till 65. The Delimitation Commission draws constituency boundaries and the ECI implements its orders; the ECI also revises rolls, schedules polls, registers and recognises parties, frames and enforces the non-statutory Model Code and acts as a tribunal on recognition and symbol disputes. Disqualification advice goes to the President (MPs) or the Governor (State legislators). The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge, other Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation; in Anoop Baranwal (2023) the Court directed an interim PM-LoP-CJI appointment committee.
concepts.example: A Commissioner other than the CEC cannot be dismissed by the government unless the CEC recommends it.

questions.q: Which one of the following elections lies outside the superintendence, direction and control that Article 324 vests in the Election Commission of India?
questions.a: Elections to a Municipal Corporation, which a State Election Commission conducts under Article 243ZA
o: Elections to a Municipal Corporation, which a State Election Commission conducts under Article 243ZA
Elections to a State Legislative Council from the graduates' constituencies
Election to the office of the Vice-President of India by the electoral college
Election to the Rajya Sabha from a State by the members of the Legislative Assembly
questions.e: Article 324 covers the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and Councils, and the offices of President and Vice-President; Panchayat and Municipal polls are conducted by State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
w: State Legislative Councils are covered by Article 324.
The offices of President and Vice-President are covered by Article 324.
Rajya Sabha elections are covered by Article 324.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the Election Commission of India under Article 324 of the Constitution?
questions.a: A Chief Election Commissioner and as many other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix
o: A Chief Election Commissioner and as many other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix
A Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners, a number fixed by Article 324 itself
A Chief Election Commissioner and such number of Election Commissioners as Parliament may fix by law from time to time
A Chief Election Commissioner alone, with additional Commissioners appointable only through a constitutional amendment
questions.e: Article 324 provides for the CEC plus such other ECs, if any, as the President fixes; the CEC chairs the Commission when others are appointed.records the single-member Commission till 1989 and the three-member form since 1993.
w: Article 324 leaves the strength to the President; the present three-member form is a matter of practice.
The number is fixed by the President, not by a Parliamentary law, though Parliament may regulate appointment and service.
Additional Commissioners can be appointed by the President directly; the Commission was multi-member in 1989 and again from 1993.

questions.q: Constituency boundaries for the Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections in India are drawn by
questions.a: a Delimitation Commission constituted under a law of Parliament, whose orders the Election Commission then implements
o: a Delimitation Commission constituted under a law of Parliament, whose orders the Election Commission then implements
the Election Commission itself, acting under Article 324 on the advice of the Registrar General of India
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the Election Commission
the State Election Commissions acting jointly under Articles 243K and 243ZA
questions.e: The ECI's role is supervisory: the boundaries are drawn by the Delimitation Commission created under Parliament's Delimitation Acts, and the ECI operationalises the orders once they have legal force.
w: The ECI does not draw boundaries on its own; it assists the Delimitation Commission and gives effect to its orders.
The Speaker has no role in drawing constituencies.
State Election Commissions deal only with Panchayat and Municipal elections.

questions.q: When rival groups of a recognised party each claim its name and its election symbol, the dispute is decided by the Election Commission of India acting as
questions.a: a tribunal, because the Commission settles disputes on recognition of parties and allotment of symbols
o: a tribunal, because the Commission settles disputes on recognition of parties and allotment of symbols
an election court, because it hears petitions challenging the validity of the election of a returned candidate
a Delimitation Commission, because it settles which constituency a party may contest
an advisory body to the Speaker, because the Tenth Schedule makes it the authority on splits and mergers
questions.e: Among its quasi-judicial functions the ECI acts as a tribunal on disputes about recognition of political parties and allotment of symbols, and appoints inquiry officers for electoral disputes.
w: Election petitions on validity of elections go to the High Court, not the ECI.
Constituency boundaries are not the subject of a party-name dispute.
The Tenth Schedule is decided by the presiding officer; the ECI's tribunal role concerns recognition and symbols.

questions.q: A person is appointed Chief Election Commissioner at the age of 61 years. Under the law governing the service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners, his tenure will end
questions.a: at the age of 65 years, because that limit is reached before six years in office
o: at the age of 65 years, because that limit is reached before six years in office
after six years in office, when he is 67 years old
at the age of 62 years, the limit that applies to State Public Service Commission members
after five years in office, when he is 66 years old
questions.e: The CEC and ECs hold office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier; four years from 61 reaches 65 first. They may resign in writing to the President.
w: Six years would take him past 65, and the earlier limit governs.
62 years is the limit for State Public Service Commission members, not Election Commissioners.
The term is not five years, and the age cap of 65 still applies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scope of the Election Commission of India:

1. It is a permanent and independent body created directly by the Constitution under Article 324.
2. It also conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities with the State Election Commissions acting as its agents.
3. Its superintendence covers elections to the Rajya Sabha and to State Legislative Councils as well as to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
4. It controls elections to the offices of the President and the Vice-President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 324 creates a permanent, independent constitutional body. Statement 2 is incorrect: State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA conduct local-body elections themselves; the ECI does not. Statement 3 is correct: Article 324 covers both Houses of Parliament and both Houses of State Legislatures. Statement 4 is correct: These two offices are within Article 324.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of members of the Election Commission:

1. The number of Election Commissioners besides the Chief Election Commissioner is fixed by the President from time to time.
2. Article 324 itself fixes the strength of the Commission at three, namely the CEC and two Election Commissioners.
3. When any other Election Commissioner is appointed, the Chief Election Commissioner acts as the chairman of the Commission.
4. Article 324 lays down a detailed procedure for the appointment of the CEC and ECs, so Parliament has no power to legislate on the subject.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 324 leaves the number to the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 324 fixes no number; the Commission has been multi-member in practice since 1993. Statement 3 is correct: The CEC chairs the multi-member Commission. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 324 gives no detailed procedure and Parliament may legislate on appointment.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tenure and service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners:

1. Each member's tenure ends at the completion of six years or on reaching the age of 65, whichever comes first.
2. They may resign at any time, and may also be removed before the end of the term in the constitutional manner.
3. Their conditions of service and tenure are determined by the President, subject to any law made by Parliament.
4. The Constitution neither prescribes qualifications of the members of the Commission nor bars a retiring Commissioner from further government appointment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the statute on their appointment and service conditions fixes six years or age 65, whichever is earlier. Statement 2 is correct: resignation and constitutional removal are both open. Statement 3 is correct: Article 324(5) leaves their service conditions and tenure to the President, subject to any law made by Parliament. Statement 4 is correct: the Constitution prescribes no qualifications for the members and does not bar post-retirement government appointments; both are recognised gaps in safeguarding the Commission's independence.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: they can resign and can be removed in the constitutional manner.
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: the term is six years or age 65, whichever is earlier.
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: Article 324(5) vests this in the President, subject to Parliament's law.
tr: Term from a law, not Article 324

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative functions of the Election Commission of India:

1. It prepares and periodically revises electoral rolls and registers eligible voters, including through Special Intensive Revision when required.
2. It notifies the dates and schedule of elections and scrutinises nomination papers, accepting or rejecting candidatures.
3. It can countermand a poll for rigging, booth capturing or violence only after obtaining the prior approval of the President.
4. It registers political parties for the purpose of elections under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Roll preparation and revision is an administrative function. Statement 2 is correct: Scheduling and scrutiny of nominations are listed functions. Statement 3 is incorrect: The ECI itself cancels or countermands polls for such irregularities; no Presidential approval is required. Statement 4 is correct: Registration of parties is under the 1951 Act.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission, political parties and the Model Code of Conduct:

1. The ECI recognises parties as National or State parties on the basis of their electoral performance.
2. Election symbols are allotted to parties under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
3. The Model Code of Conduct is a statute enacted by Parliament, and a violation is tried as an offence under that statute.
4. The ECI prepares a roster for the equitable publicity of parties on All India Radio and Doordarshan.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Recognition follows poll performance. Statement 2 is incorrect: Symbols are allotted under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Code is non-statutory; the ECI enforces it through its Article 324 powers. Statement 4 is correct: The roster for publicity on AIR and Doordarshan is a listed function.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the advisory and quasi-judicial functions of the Election Commission:

1. On the disqualification of a Member of Parliament, the ECI gives its opinion to the Speaker or the Chairman of the House concerned.
2. The ECI advises the President on whether elections can be held in a State under President's Rule.
3. The ECI hears election petitions challenging the validity of the election of a returned candidate and is the final authority on them.
4. The ECI appoints inquiry officers for electoral disputes and for complaints about election arrangements.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The ECI advises the President on disqualification of MPs and the Governor on disqualification of State legislators. Statement 2 is correct: It is a listed advisory function, judged on law and order and administrative feasibility. Statement 3 is incorrect: Election petitions are heard by the High Court; the ECI's tribunal function concerns party recognition and symbols. Statement 4 is correct: Appointing inquiry officers is listed as a quasi-judicial function.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the machinery that assists the Election Commission:

1. Deputy Election Commissioners are drawn from the senior civil services and are appointed by the President.
2. The Chief Electoral Officer of a State is appointed by the ECI in consultation with the State Government.
3. At the district level, the District Collector usually acts as the District Election Officer or District Returning Officer.
4. The Presiding Officer of a polling station is appointed directly by the Election Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: They are appointed by the Commission itself. Statement 2 is correct: This is the rule for the State-level officer. Statement 3 is correct: The Collector usually holds this post. Statement 4 is incorrect: the district returning officer appoints Returning Officers and Presiding Officers; the ECI does not appoint them directly.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of Election Commissioners:

1. The Chief Election Commissioner has the same security of tenure as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. A motion for his removal needs adoption by both Houses by a majority of the total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. The grounds are proved misbehaviour or incapacity, neither of which the Constitution defines.
4. Other Election Commissioners may be removed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 324 gives the CEC judge-like protection. Statement 2 is correct: This is the special majority used for a Supreme Court judge. Statement 3 is correct: The Constitution gives no definition for the Commission, unlike the Public Service Commissions. Statement 4 is incorrect: They cannot be removed except on the recommendation of the CEC.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), the Supreme Court declared the following about the Election Commission. Consider the statements:

1. The Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners are to be appointed on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
2. The Court's directions are to remain in force permanently, even after Parliament makes a law in consonance with Article 324.
3. It is desirable that the grounds of removal of the other Election Commissioners be the same as for the CEC, subject to the CEC's recommendation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Court named the Chief Justice of India as the third member; the Cabinet Minister came later in the 2023 Act. Statement 2 is incorrect: They were to operate only until Parliament makes such a law. Statement 3 is correct: The Court called this desirable.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

1. The Constitution prescribes the legal, educational, administrative or judicial qualifications of the Election Commissioners.
2. The Constitution bars retiring Election Commissioners from any further appointment by the Government.
3. The President may, after consulting the Election Commission, appoint regional commissioners to assist it.
4. The Commission functioned as a single-member body from its inception in 1950 until October 1989.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Constitution prescribes no qualifications. Statement 2 is incorrect: it has not debarred retiring Commissioners from further appointment. Statement 3 is correct: Article 324 permits regional commissioners after consultation. Statement 4 is correct: it was a single-member body till 15 October 1989. So exactly 2 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission's dealings with political parties:

1. The Commission acts as a tribunal in disputes about recognition of parties and allotment of symbols.
2. Symbols are allotted under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1951.
3. The Model Code of Conduct derives its binding force from a specific section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
4. Political parties are registered by the Commission under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: A listed quasi-judicial function. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Order is of 1968. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is non-statutory and rests on Article 324 powers. Statement 4 is incorrect: Registration is under the 1951 Act. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission's functions and officers:

1. Its functions are classed as administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial.
2. It assists the Delimitation Commission and implements the Commission's orders once they have legal force.
3. The Presiding Officer, and not the Returning Officer, declares the result of an election in a constituency.
4. It asks the President or the Governor to requisition civil servants, police and other staff needed for election duty.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the classification in the chapter. Statement 2 is correct: The ECI enforces; the Delimitation Commission draws. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Returning Officer handles nomination scrutiny, polling, counting and declaration of results. Statement 4 is correct: Requisitioning staff is a listed function. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Election Commission can countermand a poll in a constituency where booth capturing or violence has occurred.
Statement-II: The Election Commission is the authority to which the Constitution entrusts the overall management of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Power to superintend, direct and control elections is the source of the power to cancel a poll for irregularities.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Other Election Commissioners cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Statement-II: Article 324 gives the other Election Commissioners the same impeachment-type protection that the Chief Election Commissioner enjoys.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is incorrect. Statement-I is the rule in Article 324; Statement-II is incorrect because the judge-like protection belongs to the CEC alone, which is why the protection is called hierarchical.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I
Statement-II is incorrect, not merely non-explanatory
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Match the officers in List-I with the correct descriptions in List-II.

List-I
A. Deputy Election Commissioner
B. Chief Electoral Officer
C. District Election Officer (District Returning Officer)
D. Presiding Officer

List-II
1. Conducts voting at a polling station and ensures secrecy and fairness
2. Usually the District Collector
3. Appointed by the ECI in consultation with the State Government
4. Drawn from the senior civil services and appointed by the Commission
questions.e: Deputy Election Commissioners come from the senior civil services and are appointed by the Commission; the CEO is appointed by the ECI in consultation with the State Government; the Collector is usually the DEO/DRO; the Presiding Officer runs a polling station.
w: A and B are interchanged.
C and D are interchanged.
A and C are interchanged.

concepts.name: Electoral reforms, the ECI summary table and the CAG: articles, independence and functions
concepts.description: Criminalisation, funding, paid news, Model Code issues, exit polls, reform proposals, the 2023 appointment Act, the CAG articles 148-151 and 279, independence and audit functions.
concepts.idea: Electoral reform debates, the ECI at a glance and the CAG's constitutional protections and audit jurisdiction.
concepts.rule: Lily Thomas (2013) struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA so that a convicted legislator is disqualified at once; Electoral Bonds were struck down in February 2024. The Model Code applies only from the announcement of elections, and Section 126A bans exit polls. Under the 2023 Act the CEC and ECs are appointed on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, the Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister. The CAG (Article 148) is appointed by warrant, removable like a Supreme Court judge, barred from further office, and audits Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds and Public Accounts, stores, revenue and bodies substantially financed by the Government; Articles 149, 150, 151 and 279 cover duties, form of accounts, reports and net proceeds.
concepts.example: A CAG who retires cannot be appointed to any State office.

questions.q: The Chief Election Commissioner is removed in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court. In practice this means removal
questions.a: by the President on a motion adopted by both Houses, each by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting, for proved misbehaviour or incapacity
o: by the President on a motion adopted by both Houses, each by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting, for proved misbehaviour or incapacity
by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers, whenever the Prime Minister loses confidence in him on account of his decisions on electoral matters
by the Chief Justice of India after an inquiry by a committee of three Judges of the Supreme Court, followed by a report to the President
by the President on a resolution of the Lok Sabha alone, passed by a simple majority of the members present and voting, on any ground of misconduct
questions.e: The CEC cannot be removed except in the manner and on the grounds of a Supreme Court judge: a motion of both Houses with the special majority, on proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
w: The CEC does not hold office at the pleasure of the President or the Prime Minister.
The Chief Justice has no power of removal; Parliament acts through the special majority.
Both Houses and a special majority are required, not a simple majority in one House.

questions.q: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. As a result, a sitting MP or MLA who is convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for two years or more
questions.a: stands disqualified immediately, without the protection of a pending appeal
o: stands disqualified immediately, without the protection of a pending appeal
continues to sit for three months, and beyond that period if an appeal is filed within it
is disqualified only after the appellate court has confirmed the conviction
is disqualified only if the offence is one involving moral turpitude
questions.e: Section 8(4) let a sitting member continue while an appeal was pending; Lily Thomas (2013) struck it down, so conviction with a sentence of two years or more disqualifies at once.
w: That was exactly the protection Section 8(4) gave, which the Court struck down.
Disqualification follows conviction and sentence; it does not wait for the appeal.
The two-year sentence rule is not restricted to offences involving moral turpitude.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as the office works in practice?
questions.a: Authorising the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India before it is spent
o: Authorising the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India before it is spent
Advising the President on the form in which the accounts of the Union and the States are to be kept
Acting as the guide, friend and philosopher of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament
Auditing the expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of each State
questions.e: The Constitution visualises a Comptroller as well as Auditor-General, but in practice the CAG works only as Auditor-General: he has no control over issue of money from the Consolidated Fund and acts at the audit stage.
w: Article 150 gives the CAG this advisory role.
The CAG is the principal technical adviser of the Public Accounts Committee.
State Consolidated Fund expenditure is within his audit.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India makes and subscribes the oath or affirmation of office before
questions.a: the President or a person appointed by the President
o: the President or a person appointed by the President
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha in the presence of the Prime Minister
the Prime Minister of India or any Cabinet Minister he nominates
the Attorney General of India as the first law officer of the Union
questions.e: The CAG is appointed by the President by warrant and takes the oath before the President or a person the President appoints.
w: The Speaker has no role in the CAG's oath.
The Prime Minister does not administer it.
The Attorney General is not the authority; the oath is taken before the President or his appointee.

questions.q: On ceasing to hold office, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is
questions.a: not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or the Government of any State
o: not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or the Government of any State
eligible for reappointment as CAG for one more term, provided both Houses of Parliament approve it
ineligible for office under the Union but eligible for office under a State Government
free to accept any office after a cooling-off period of two years
questions.e: Article 148 bars the CAG from any further office under the Union or a State after he leaves office.
w: A second term as CAG is itself a further office barred by Article 148.
The bar covers both the Union and the States.
The Constitution prescribes no cooling-off period; the bar is absolute.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about criminalisation of politics and the steps taken against it:

1. The causes cited for criminalisation include low conviction rates and the first-past-the-post system, under which a candidate can win without securing a majority of the votes.
2. In Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India (2018) the Supreme Court barred persons against whom charges had been framed for a serious offence from contesting elections.
3. The Law Commission's 244th Report recommended a stiffer penalty for false affidavits under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Both are among the causes listed. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Court left disqualification on framing of charges to Parliament and instead directed wide publicity of criminal antecedents. Statement 3 is correct: Penalty for false affidavits was among its proposals.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about political funding in India:

1. Individual donations (Section 29B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951) and corporate funding (the Companies Act, 2013) are recognised sources of party funds.
2. Electoral Bonds were bearer instruments that allowed donors to give to parties anonymously.
3. The Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme in February 2024 in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India.
4. The Finance Act, 2017 subjected donations received through Electoral Bonds to the same disclosure norms of the Representation of the People Act as other donations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: These are the two legal private sources named. Statement 2 is correct: Anonymity of donors was the central feature. Statement 3 is correct: The scheme is no longer valid. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Act exempted them from the disclosure norms, which was a ground of criticism.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about paid news and the Election Commission:

1. The Press Council of India defines paid news as news or analysis published for a consideration in cash or kind.
2. The Election Commission responds through Media Certification and Monitoring Committees that track the notional expenditure of candidates on advertisements.
3. The Media Certification and Monitoring Committees are constituted by the Press Council of India at the district level.
4. Causes listed for paid news include corporatisation of the media, weakened editorial autonomy and low wages of journalists.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the Council's definition. Statement 2 is correct: MCMCs work at district and State level. Statement 3 is incorrect: They are set up by the Election Commission, not by the Press Council. Statement 4 is correct: These are the causes listed.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct:

1. The Code covers general conduct, meetings, processions, polling day and the conduct of the party in power, and since 2013 it also covers election manifestos.
2. In S. Subramaniam Balaji v. Government of Tamil Nadu (2013) the Supreme Court held that a promise of freebies in a manifesto is a corrupt practice under the Representation of the People Act.
3. The Code comes into force on the day the House is dissolved, so government advertisements are barred from that day.
4. The guidelines on manifestos expect parties to explain the rationale of their promises and to indicate the means of financing them.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The manifesto part was added in 2013. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Court did not treat manifesto promises as corrupt practice; it asked the ECI to frame guidelines, which led to the manifesto part of the Code. Statement 3 is incorrect: It applies only from the announcement of elections, which lets the ruling party release government advertisements just before. Statement 4 is correct: This is the content of the manifesto guidelines.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about exit polls and proposals for strengthening the Election Commission:

1. Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 bans the conduct and publication of exit polls only during the 48 hours before the close of polling in each phase.
2. Section 126A is aimed at exit polls and does not itself ban opinion polls.
3. It has been proposed that Article 324(5) be amended to withdraw the judge-like removal protection of the Chief Election Commissioner and place him on par with other Election Commissioners.
4. It has been proposed that the Commission's budget be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, as is done for the Supreme Court and the CAG.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The ban runs from the start of polling till half an hour after the last phase ends. Statement 2 is correct: Opinion polls are not covered by this provision. Statement 3 is incorrect: The proposal is the reverse: to give the other two Commissioners the same protection as the CEC. Statement 4 is correct: This would insulate it from the annual vote.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional Articles relating to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. Article 148 provides for an independent CAG appointed by the President by warrant, whose expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Under Article 150 the form in which the accounts of the Union and the States are kept is prescribed by the CAG with the approval of Parliament.
3. Under Article 151 the audit reports on Union accounts go to the President, who has them laid before Parliament, and those on State accounts go to the Governor.
4. Under Article 279 the CAG ascertains and certifies the net proceeds of a tax, and his certificate is final.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Appointment, independence and expenses are in Article 148. Statement 2 is incorrect: The President prescribes the form on the advice of the CAG. Statement 3 is correct: Article 151 provides the route of the reports. Statement 4 is correct: The certificate is final and binding.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the independence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. He can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds of a Supreme Court judge, that is by a special majority of Parliament for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
2. His salary and service conditions are determined by Parliament, and his salary, leave, pension and retirement age cannot be altered to his disadvantage after appointment.
3. The conditions of service of persons in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and his administrative powers are prescribed by the President after consulting him.
4. He holds office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Removal is hedged like a judge's. Statement 2 is correct: Until Parliament legislated they stood in the Second Schedule. Statement 3 is correct: This is the rule-making route, subject to Parliament's laws. Statement 4 is correct: He holds office for six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the audit functions of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. He audits the Contingency Fund and Public Account of India but not those of the States.
2. He audits the stores and stock of government offices and checks that revenue is properly assessed, collected and allocated.
3. He audits expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of each State and of each Union Territory having a Legislative Assembly.
4. He audits bodies and authorities substantially financed from Central or State revenues, and Government companies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Contingency Fund and Public Account of each State are also audited. Statement 2 is correct: Both are listed duties. Statement 3 is correct: Union Territories with Legislative Assemblies are included. Statement 4 is correct: Both are within his audit.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the working of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. In practice he exercises the functions of both a Comptroller and an Auditor-General, as his British counterpart does.
2. For secret service expenditure he cannot call for particulars but must accept a certificate from the competent administrative authority.
3. Since 1976 he has been relieved of compiling and maintaining the accounts of the Central Government, while he still compiles and maintains those of the State Governments.
4. Performance audit was brought within his scope by an amendment to the Constitution in 2006.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: In practice he works only as Auditor-General; in Britain the executive can draw money only with the approval of the CAG. Statement 2 is correct: Secret service expenditure is a limit on his audit. Statement 3 is correct: This followed the separation of accounts from audit. Statement 4 is incorrect: It was clarified by a 2006 Office Memorandum of the Ministry of Finance, not a constitutional amendment.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about electoral reforms:

1. A Parliamentary Standing Committee recommended that the Model Code of Conduct be made legally binding by incorporating it in the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. The Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme in November 2023.
3. India provides direct State funding of elections through a National Election Fund.
4. A permanent, separate secretariat for the Election Commission, like those of the two Houses of Parliament, has been suggested.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Code applies only from announcement of elections and has no statutory force. Statement 2 is incorrect: The judgment was in February 2024. Statement 3 is incorrect: Direct State funding is not provided; indirect support such as free media access exists. Statement 4 is correct: The Law Commission suggestion is on these lines. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. He holds office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. He holds office during the pleasure of the President, who may remove him at will.
3. Until Parliament legislated, his salary and conditions of service were those specified in the Second Schedule.
4. He makes and subscribes his oath of office before the President or a person appointed by the President.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is his term. Statement 2 is incorrect: Only the Supreme Court-judge procedure removes him. Statement 3 is correct: Article 148 provides this. Statement 4 is correct: That is the prescribed authority. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:

1. It is a permanent and independent constitutional body, not a statutory body.
2. The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners is five years, or retirement at 65 if that comes earlier.
3. Under the 2023 Act the selection committee that recommends appointments includes the Chief Justice of India.
4. Under the 2023 Act the salary of the Commissioners is equal to that of a Supreme Court judge.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is created by Article 324. Statement 2 is incorrect: The term is six years or age 65, whichever is earlier. Statement 3 is incorrect: The 2023 Act names a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister; the Chief Justice was in the Court's interim arrangement. Statement 4 is incorrect: The 1991 Act equated it with a Supreme Court judge; the 2023 Act aligned it with the Cabinet Secretary. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A sitting MP or MLA convicted and sentenced to two years or more is now disqualified from the date of conviction.
Statement-II: In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) the Supreme Court struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which had protected sitting members pending appeal.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The removal of the Section 8(4) shield is the reason the disqualification now operates at once.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The service conditions of the Comptroller and Auditor General cannot be altered to his disadvantage after his appointment.
Statement-II: The administrative expenses of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Both are true provisions of Article 148 and its implementing arrangements, but charged expenses concern voting by Parliament, not the protection of the incumbent's conditions.
w: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I; it is a separate point
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Match the constitutional provisions on the CAG in List-I with what they deal with in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 149
B. Article 150
C. Article 151
D. Article 279

List-II
1. Certificate of the net proceeds of a tax, which is final
2. Audit reports submitted to the President or the Governor and laid before the legislature
3. Duties and powers of the CAG prescribed by Parliament by law
4. Form of Union and State accounts prescribed by the President on the CAG's advice
questions.e: Article 149 leaves duties and powers to Parliament; Article 150 the form of accounts; Article 151 the audit reports; Article 279 the net proceeds certificate.
w: A and B are interchanged.
C and D are interchanged.
A and C are interchanged.

concepts.name: CAG reports and issues, the Finance Commission and the composition of the UPSC
concepts.description: The three audit reports, issues and reform ideas for the CAG, types of audit, the Finance Commission's composition and functions, and the UPSC's composition and tenure.
concepts.idea: The CAG's reports, audit types and reform debates, the Finance Commission under Article 280 and the constitution of the UPSC.
concepts.rule: According to Laxmikanth the CAG submits reports on appropriation accounts, finance accounts and public undertakings; legal and regulatory audit is obligatory, propriety audit discretionary, and performance audit was clarified in 2006. The Finance Commission (Article 280) has a chairman with public-affairs experience and four members from four listed groups, is constituted afresh every fifth year and makes advisory recommendations on devolution, grants-in-aid and local-body resources; the Sixteenth is chaired by Arvind Panagariya. The UPSC is created by Articles 315-323, its members are appointed by the President, at least half must have ten years' government service, and they hold office for six years or till 65.
concepts.example: A State cannot sue the Union to force payment of a grant the Finance Commission recommended.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General submits three audit reports to the President. The one that compares the actual expenditure of the year with the sums sanctioned by Parliament through the Appropriation Act is the audit report on
questions.e: The three reports are on Appropriation Accounts (actual versus sanctioned expenditure), Finance Accounts (receipts and disbursements) and Public Undertakings; the President lays them before both Houses and the Public Accounts Committee examines them. The 'three reports' rest on practice and the 1971 Act rather than Article 151, which requires reports generally.
w: Finance Accounts present the annual receipts and disbursements of the Union Government, not the comparison with sanctions.
The report on public undertakings deals with government-owned enterprises.
Revenue Receipts is not one of the three reports named and does not compare expenditure with sanctions.

questions.q: The Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Constitution is best described as
questions.a: a non-permanent quasi-judicial constitutional body constituted afresh every fifth year or earlier if necessary
o: a non-permanent quasi-judicial constitutional body constituted afresh every fifth year or earlier if necessary
a permanent statutory body of experts that Parliament reviews and then reconstitutes in every fifth year by law
a permanent quasi-judicial constitutional body whose members each hold office for a fixed term of five years
a statutory advisory body that Parliament constitutes by law once in every five years or earlier
questions.e: Article 280 makes the President constitute a Finance Commission every five years or earlier; it ceases after submitting its report, with its term set in the Presidential order.
w: It is neither permanent nor statutory; it is created by the Constitution and ceases after reporting.
Members hold office for the period fixed in the President's order, and the Commission is reconstituted each time.
It is constituted by the President, not by Parliament, and the Constitution itself provides for it.

questions.q: The Finance Commission has a chairman and four other members. Which one of the following is NOT among the categories from which Parliament has provided that the four other members are selected?
questions.a: A person having experience in public affairs
o: A person having experience in public affairs
A judge of a High Court or one qualified to be appointed as one
A person with special knowledge of the finance and accounts of the government
A person with special knowledge of economics
questions.e: The chairman must have experience in public affairs; the four members come from the four groups of High Court judge, finance and accounts expert, person with wide financial and administrative experience, and economist.
w: A High Court judge, or a person qualified to be appointed as one, is the first of the four member categories.
Special knowledge of the finance and accounts of the government is one of the four member categories.
Special knowledge of economics is the last of the four member categories.

questions.q: No qualifications are prescribed for membership of the Union Public Service Commission, except that
questions.a: one-half of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government
o: one-half of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government
one-third of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government
one-half of the members must have held office for at least five years under the Government of India or a State Government
all members must have served as officers of the All India Services for at least ten years under the Union
questions.e: Article 316 requires that at least half the members have held office for ten years under the Union or a State; there is no academic qualification.
w: The proportion is one-half, not one-third.
The qualifying period is ten years, not five.
Service in the All India Services is not a requirement.

questions.q: As constituted for the award period beginning in 2026, the Sixteenth Finance Commission has as its chairman
questions.e: The Sixteenth Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya and covers the period 2026-31. Among the wrong options, N.K. Singh chaired the Fifteenth Commission (2020-26).
w: N.K. Singh chaired the Fifteenth Finance Commission (2020-26).
Y.V. Reddy chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission (2015-20).
Vijay Kelkar chaired the Thirteenth Finance Commission (2010-15).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. The audit reports the CAG submits to the President are of three kinds, relating to appropriation accounts, finance accounts and public undertakings.
2. The audit reports on State accounts are laid before the State Legislature by the CAG himself, without passing through the Governor.
3. The audit report on appropriation accounts shows the annual receipts and disbursements of the Union Government.
4. After the President lays the Union reports before both Houses, the Public Accounts Committee examines them and reports its findings to Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the CAG submits these three audit reports to the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: State reports go to the Governor, who places them before the State Legislature. Statement 3 is incorrect: that describes the finance accounts; appropriation accounts compare actual with sanctioned expenditure. Statement 4 is correct: this is the follow-up route.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about issues raised regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed through a statutory selection committee that includes the Leader of Opposition.
2. In the KG Basin gas-pricing dispute, Reliance argued that the CAG cannot audit private firms working under Production Sharing Contracts.
3. CAG reports on the 2G spectrum, coal blocks and the Delhi Airport public-private partnership drew allegations that he had exceeded his mandate.
4. The Second Administrative Reforms Commission noted that grants and loans given to NGOs are rarely audited.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant, with no statutory selection committee and no fixed criteria or parliamentary role. Statement 2 is correct: that argument was the point of dispute. Statement 3 is correct: these reports drew such allegations. Statement 4 is correct: the Second ARC listed rare audit of grants and loans to NGOs among the challenges.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: Reliance did argue this in the KG Basin dispute.
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: those reports drew allegations of overreach.
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: the Second ARC did note rare audit of NGO grants and loans.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the follow-up of audit findings and about audit institutions elsewhere:

1. Members of the Public Accounts Committee have a tenure of one year, and the Committee lacks technical expertise.
2. The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are advisory in nature.
3. Excess expenditure is regularised by the CAG through a certificate under Article 205.
4. Australia and Canada have separate Auditors-General for the federal and the provincial governments.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: These are listed weaknesses. Statement 2 is correct: The executive is not bound to act on them. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 205 concerns excess grants, which the legislature must approve; the concern is that excess expenditure stays unregularised for years. Statement 4 is correct: The comparison is made in the context of reform ideas.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

1. He is a single-member constitutional authority under Article 148.
2. His salary is equal to that of a Supreme Court judge, and he is barred from any further office under the Union or a State after leaving office.
3. One reform proposal is to appoint the CAG through a selection committee of the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition, on the lines of the Central Vigilance Commission.
4. Audit reports on Union accounts go to the President, and those on State accounts go to the Chief Minister of the State concerned.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The office is one-person and constitutional. Statement 2 is correct: Both points are stated in the summary of his service conditions. Statement 3 is correct: This has been proposed to make appointment transparent. Statement 4 is incorrect: State reports go to the Governor.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the audit of corporations and companies by the Comptroller and Auditor General:

1. Some corporations are audited totally and directly by the CAG.
2. Some corporations are audited by private professional auditors appointed by the Central Government in consultation with the CAG, and the CAG can conduct a supplementary audit if necessary.
3. Some corporations are subject exclusively to private audit and submit their annual reports and accounts directly to Parliament.
4. In the case of Government companies the CAG may undertake a supplementary or test audit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is one of three categories. Statement 2 is correct: This is the second category. Statement 3 is correct: The CAG does not come into the picture at all. Statement 4 is correct: The CAG's role in company audit is limited.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the types of audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General:

1. Legal and regulatory audit, which checks that money was legally available and spent in conformity with the governing authority, is obligatory.
2. Propriety audit, which examines the wisdom, faithfulness and economy of expenditure, is discretionary.
3. Performance audit is concerned only with whether the expenditure had legal authority.
4. The CAG has the same freedom in framing audit codes for receipts, stores and stock as he has for expenditure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is a statutory duty under the 1971 Act. Statement 2 is correct: The CAG may but need not conduct it. Statement 3 is incorrect: It concerns economy, efficiency and effectiveness in receipt and application of public funds. Statement 4 is incorrect: He has more freedom for expenditure; for the other audits he proceeds with the approval of the executive.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Finance Commission:

1. The members of the Finance Commission are not eligible for reappointment.
2. Their qualifications are prescribed by Parliament through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.
3. A person convicted of any offence, however minor, is disqualified from membership.
4. A person who has such financial or other interest as is likely to prejudice the discharge of his functions as a member is disqualified.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: They are eligible for reappointment. Statement 2 is correct: Parliament was authorised to prescribe them. Statement 3 is incorrect: The disqualification is for an offence involving moral turpitude. Statement 4 is correct: This is among the grounds, with unsoundness of mind and undischarged insolvency.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the Finance Commission:

1. Horizontal devolution fixes the share of the States as a whole in the divisible pool of central taxes.
2. Grants-in-aid are extra transfers for States or sectors needing special assistance, and supplement the devolution of taxes.
3. The recommendations of the Commission are binding on the Union, and a State may enforce them in a court.
4. Any other financial matter in the interest of sound finance may be referred to it by Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: That is vertical devolution; horizontal distribution allocates the States' share among the States, and the criteria differ from one Commission to another. Statement 2 is correct: They are additional to devolution. Statement 3 is incorrect: They are advisory and create no enforceable right. Statement 4 is incorrect: The reference is made by the President.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Public Service Commission:

1. The Commission recruits to the All India Services and to the Central civil service as a whole, from Group A down to the entire Group D cadre.
2. The Constitution does not fix the strength of the Commission and leaves it to the President.
3. At least half of its members must have held office for ten years under the Union or a State Government.
4. The President determines the service conditions of its Chairman and members and may vary them to their disadvantage after appointment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It recruits to the All India Services and to Group A and Group B Central Services; the bulk of Group C and D posts is outside its jurisdiction, so it does not recruit the entire Group D cadre. Statement 2 is correct: The number of members varies in practice. Statement 3 is correct: That is the only qualification. Statement 4 is incorrect: The conditions cannot be varied to the member's disadvantage after appointment.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, with reference to the perceptions and challenges recorded by the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:

1. Because his audit is post facto, its findings may reach the executive too late for corrective action.
2. Audit Committees of audit and government agencies, set up to review action on inspection reports, are recorded as functioning satisfactorily.
3. The Public Accounts Committee examines in detail most of the 1,000 to 1,500 audit paras submitted each year.
4. His findings rest on documents and files with practically no physical verification.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: this is among the perceptions noted by the Second Administrative Reforms Commission. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Second ARC records that their functioning is not satisfactory. Statement 3 is incorrect: detailed PAC examination covers barely 15-20 of the 1,000 to 1,500 paras. Statement 4 is correct: the Second ARC records that findings rest on documents with practically no physical verification. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Public Service Commission:

1. Article 316 provides for the appointment of its Chairman and members by the President.
2. The Chairman and members hold office for six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
3. The President may appoint one of the members as acting Chairman when the office of the Chairman falls vacant or the Chairman is unable to perform his functions.
4. The Chairman or a member can resign by addressing the resignation to the President.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 316 deals with composition and appointment. Statement 2 is incorrect: The age limit is 65 for the UPSC; 62 is for State Commissions. Statement 3 is correct: The acting Chairman functions till the new Chairman joins or the Chairman resumes. Statement 4 is correct: Resignation goes to the President. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:

1. The Thirteenth Finance Commission gave grants for justice delivery and for strengthening the statistical system.
2. The Chairman of the Commission must be a person with special knowledge of economics.
3. The Fifteenth Finance Commission was chaired by Y.V. Reddy.
4. The Commission consists of a chairman and six other members.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: These were among its grants. Statement 2 is incorrect: The chairman must have experience in public affairs. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Fifteenth Commission was chaired by N.K. Singh; Y.V. Reddy chaired the Fourteenth. Statement 4 is incorrect: It consists of a chairman and four other members. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A State cannot approach a court to compel the Union to pay a grant recommended by the Finance Commission.
Statement-II: The Constitution nowhere makes the recommendations of the Finance Commission binding on the Union or gives the beneficiary State a legal right to the money recommended.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The absence of a binding force or a legal right is why no enforceable claim lies.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Union Public Service Commission is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
Statement-II: The Constitution does not fix the strength of the Union Public Service Commission and leaves it to the discretion of the President.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect. Statement-II is correct. The UPSC is created directly by Articles 315 to 323, so Statement-I is incorrect; Statement-II is a correct provision.
w: Statement-I is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect
Statement-II is correct

questions.q:
Match the Finance Commissions in List-I with their chairmen in List-II.

List-I
A. Twelfth Finance Commission
B. Thirteenth Finance Commission

D. Fifteenth Finance Commission

List-II

2. Vijay Kelkar

4. C. Rangarajan
