concepts.name: UPSC functions, State Public Service Commissions, Joint Commissions and the origin of the SC commission
concepts.description: Recruitment and consultation roles of the UPSC, its limits and report, the SPSC's composition, tenure, removal and functions, the Joint SPSC and the constitutional history of Article 338.
concepts.idea: The UPSC and State Commissions recruit and advise within limits, with the President alone removing members, while Joint Commissions are statutory.
concepts.rule: Under Article 320 the UPSC conducts examinations and is consulted on recruitment methods, principles of appointment, promotion and transfer, disciplinary matters, legal-expense reimbursement and injury pensions, but not on backward-class reservation, SC/ST claims, heads of missions or short temporary appointments; consultation is directory. A State Commission is appointed by the Governor, serves for six years or till 62, and is removed only by the President after a binding Supreme Court inquiry for misbehaviour, though the Governor may suspend. A Joint Commission is statutory, created by Parliament on State requests, its members are appointed by the President and its report goes to each Governor. Article 338 originally gave a Special Officer; the 65th Amendment (1990) created a commission and the 89th (2003) inserted Article 338-A.
concepts.example: A government that decides a disciplinary case without asking the UPSC does not invalidate its decision.

questions.q: Under Article 320(3) the Union Public Service Commission is consulted on several matters. Which one of the following is within its consultation jurisdiction?
questions.a: Disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government of India in a civil capacity
o: Disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government of India in a civil capacity
The making of reservations of appointments or posts in favour of backward classes of citizens
The claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in making appointments to services and posts
The appointment of Ambassadors and High Commissioners as heads of Indian missions abroad
questions.e: UPSC is consulted on recruitment methods, principles of appointment, promotion and transfer, disciplinary matters (with memorials and petitions), legal-expense reimbursement, injury pensions and any matter the President refers; reservations, SC/ST claims, heads of missions and the like are excluded.
w: Reservation of posts for backward classes is kept outside its jurisdiction.
The claims of SCs and STs in appointments are outside its consultation.
Heads of diplomatic and consular missions are outside its consultation.

questions.q: The Union Public Service Commission need not be consulted on the selection for a temporary or officiating appointment to a post if
questions.a: the person appointed is not likely to hold the post for more than one year and public interest requires an immediate appointment
o: the person appointed is not likely to hold the post for more than one year and public interest requires an immediate appointment
the person appointed is not likely to hold the post for more than three years and the post is of a technical or specialised nature
the person appointed is not likely to hold the post for more than six months, whatever the degree of urgency involved in the matter
the appointment is made by the Governor of a State on the advice of the Chief Minister
questions.e: Exempts temporary or officiating appointments only if the appointee is unlikely to hold the post for more than a year and reference to the UPSC would cause undue delay in a matter of public interest.
w: The limit is one year, not three, and technical character is not the test.
The limit is one year; the second condition of urgent public interest must also be met.
The Governor's role has no bearing on UPSC's consultation for Union posts.

questions.q: The annual report of the Union Public Service Commission on its performance is placed before both Houses of Parliament by the President along with
questions.a: a memorandum explaining the cases where the advice of the Commission was not accepted and the reasons for non-acceptance
o: a memorandum explaining the cases where the advice of the Commission was not accepted and the reasons for non-acceptance
a memorandum of the Comptroller and Auditor General on the expenditure incurred by the Commission and the audit objections raised
an opinion of the Attorney General of India on the legality of the advice tendered by the Commission
a report of the Department of Personnel and Training on the vacancies filled during the year through the Commission
questions.e: Article 323: the UPSC reports annually to the President, who places the report before both Houses with a memorandum on advice not accepted and the reasons.
w: The Commission's expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund; no CAG memorandum is laid with the report.
No opinion of the Attorney General is attached.
The memorandum concerns advice not accepted, not vacancy statistics.

questions.q: A chairman or member of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor. For misbehaviour he can be removed
questions.a: by the President, after the Supreme Court has inquired and advised removal, and the advice is binding on the President
o: by the President, after the Supreme Court has inquired and advised removal, and the advice is binding on the President
by the Governor, after an inquiry conducted by the High Court of the State concerned
by the Governor on the advice of the State Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister
by the President after an inquiry by the High Court of the State, whose advice is binding on the President
questions.e: Under Article 317 a State Commission member is removed by the President, on the same grounds and in the same manner as a UPSC member; for misbehaviour the Supreme Court inquires and its advice binds the President, while the Governor may suspend the member during the inquiry.
w: The Governor appoints but cannot remove; removal is the President's.
The Council of Ministers has no role in removal.
The inquiry is held by the Supreme Court, not the High Court.

questions.q: A Joint State Public Service Commission for two or more States is
questions.a: a statutory body created by an act of Parliament on the request of the State Legislatures
o: a statutory body created by an act of Parliament on the request of the State Legislatures
a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution, like the UPSC and the State Commissions
a statutory body created by a joint law passed by the State Legislatures concerned
a constitutional body created by the Inter-State Council on the request of the Governors concerned
questions.e: The Constitution provides for a Joint State Public Service Commission, but it comes into being when the State Legislatures pass resolutions and Parliament makes a law; hence it is statutory.
w: The UPSC and SPSC are created by the Constitution; the Joint Commission is not.
States cannot create it; Parliament does so by law after the Legislatures pass resolutions.
The Inter-State Council has no role in creating it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the recruitment role of the Union Public Service Commission:

1. Article 320(1) makes it responsible for conducting examinations for appointments to the public services of the Union.
2. On a joint request from two or more States, it may help frame and operate recruitment schemes for services needing specialised qualifications.
3. It may serve the needs of a State on the request of the Governor, and the approval of the President is not required.
4. It recruits for the public services of Union Territories administered by the Union, besides the All India Services and Group A and B Central Services.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the basic recruiting function. Statement 2 is correct: This is a recognised function. Statement 3 is incorrect: The approval of the President is needed. Statement 4 is correct: These Territories fall within its recruiting field.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the matters on which the Union Public Service Commission is consulted:

1. It is consulted on methods of recruitment and on the principles to be followed in appointments, promotions and transfers from one service to another.
2. It is consulted on the classification of services, pay and cadre management.
3. It is consulted on claims for reimbursement of legal expenses incurred in defending proceedings for official acts, and on pensions for injuries sustained in service.
4. It is consulted on the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of backward classes of citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: these fall under Article 320(3). Statement 2 is incorrect: classification of services, pay and cadre management are handled by the Department of Personnel and Training, not by UPSC. Statement 3 is correct: Article 320(3) covers claims for costs of defending legal proceedings for official acts and claims for pension for injuries sustained in service. Statement 4 is incorrect: reservation for backward classes is kept outside its consultative jurisdiction.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the scope and reporting of the Union Public Service Commission:

1. It assesses the suitability of officers for promotion, transfer and deputation, notably through Departmental Promotion Committees.
2. Under Article 321 the executive may extend its functions by an order.
3. Under Article 323 it submits its annual report to the Prime Minister, who lays it before Parliament.
4. The report is laid with a memorandum explaining the cases where its advice was not accepted and the reasons for non-acceptance.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: This is one of its advisory tasks. Statement 2 is incorrect: Only Parliament can extend its functions, by law. Statement 3 is incorrect: The report goes to the President, who lays it before both Houses. Statement 4 is correct: This accompanies the report.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the independence of the Union Public Service Commission:

1. The Chairman or a member can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds mentioned in the Constitution, and the conditions of service cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
2. The Chairman and members hold office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
3. The Constitution itself fixes the strength of the Commission at a chairman and nine other members.
4. A member who has completed his first term is eligible for reappointment as a member for a second term.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Security of tenure and protected conditions. Statement 2 is correct: The term is six years or age 65, whichever is earlier. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Constitution leaves the strength of the Commission to the discretion of the President. Statement 4 is incorrect: A member is not eligible for a second term in that office.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the State Public Service Commission:

1. The State Commission is governed by Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV and does at the State level what the UPSC does for the Union.
2. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
3. The Governor decides its strength and the service conditions of its members, and at least half of the members must have held office for ten years under the Government of India or a State.
4. The Governor may appoint a member as acting Chairman when the chair is vacant or the Chairman is unable to act, and a member resigns by writing to the Governor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The same Articles govern both. Statement 2 is incorrect: They are appointed by the Governor. Statement 3 is correct: No academic qualifications are prescribed. Statement 4 is correct: The acting Chairman serves until the new Chairman joins or the Chairman resumes.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tenure and removal of members of a State Public Service Commission:

1. The Chairman and members hold office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
2. The age limit of 62 years replaced an earlier limit of 60 years through the 41st Amendment Act of 1976.
3. They are removable only by the President, who needs the binding advice of the Supreme Court after an inquiry where misbehaviour is alleged.
4. The Governor may suspend the concerned Chairman or member during the Supreme Court's inquiry.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the age limit is 62; 65 applies to the UPSC. Statement 2 is correct: the 41st Amendment Act, 1976 raised the age limit for State Commission members from 60 to 62. Statement 3 is correct: the Governor cannot remove them; only the President can, after the Supreme Court's inquiry. Statement 4 is correct: under Article 317(2) the Governor may suspend the member pending the President's order.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the State Public Service Commission:

1. It conducts competitive examinations for State civil services and State subordinate services, and is consulted on methods of recruitment and the principles of appointment, promotion and transfer.
2. It is consulted on disciplinary matters affecting a State civil servant, and on claims for reimbursement of legal expenses and for injury pensions.
3. The Governor consults it, along with the High Court, while framing rules for appointment to the judicial service of the State other than the posts of district judges.
4. The State Legislature can by law give it additional functions and bring the personnel system of local authorities or statutory corporations within its jurisdiction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: These are its core roles. Statement 2 is correct: These match the UPSC list. Statement 3 is correct: District judges are excluded. Statement 4 is correct: Its jurisdiction can be extended by a State law.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the standing of the State Public Service Commission and its advice:

1. A government decision taken without consulting the Commission is invalid, because consultation is mandatory.
2. Selection by the Commission gives no absolute right to appointment, but the State must act fairly and not arbitrarily or with mala fides.
3. The Commission reports annually to the Governor, who lays the report with a memorandum on advice not accepted, giving reasons, before the State Legislature.
4. The advice of the Commission binds the State Government, which cannot depart from it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Consultation is directory and the decision is not invalidated. Statement 2 is correct: Selection creates no vested right. Statement 3 is correct: The memorandum explains non-acceptance. Statement 4 is incorrect: The advice is not binding, though the government should act fairly and give reasons for deviation.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Joint State Public Service Commission:

1. It is a constitutional body, like the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions.
2. It is created when two or more State Legislatures pass resolutions and Parliament then makes a law on its establishment.
3. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the Governors of the participating States.
4. It sends its annual report to each participating Governor, who places it before the State Legislature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is a statutory body created by Parliament. Statement 2 is correct: It is an instance of cooperative federalism. Statement 3 is incorrect: They are appointed by the President. Statement 4 is correct: The report is not laid before Parliament.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Joint State Public Service Commission:

1. Its Chairman and members hold office for six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
2. Its members may be suspended or removed by the Governors of the participating States.
3. It is created by an Act of Parliament on the request of the State Legislatures concerned, and is therefore a statutory and not a constitutional body.
4. Its annual report is laid before Parliament by the President.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the term. Statement 2 is incorrect: Only the President may suspend or remove them. Statement 3 is correct: Parliament creates it by law on the request of the State Legislatures concerned. Statement 4 is incorrect: The report goes to each participating Governor and is laid before the State Legislature. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the matters outside the consultation jurisdiction of the Union Public Service Commission:

1. The UPSC is not consulted when reservations of appointments or posts are made in favour of backward classes of citizens.
2. The UPSC is not consulted on appointments to the posts of heads of diplomatic and consular missions abroad.
3. The UPSC is not consulted on appointments to the posts of chairman and members of boards, commissions and tribunals.
4. Presidential regulations excluding matters from consultation stay in force for good once they have been laid before Parliament for 30 days.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Excluded. Statement 2 is correct: Excluded. Statement 3 is correct: Excluded. Statement 4 is incorrect: The regulations are laid for at least 14 days and Parliament may amend or repeal them. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional history of the commission for the Scheduled Castes:

1. Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, designated the Commissioner for SCs and STs.
2. The 65th Amendment Act of 1990 inserted Article 338-A in the Constitution.
3. In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Manbodhan Lal Srivastava (1957) the Supreme Court held consultation with the Public Service Commission to be mandatory.
4. The 89th Amendment Act of 2003 amended Article 338 again and replaced the commission by a single Commissioner.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That was the original arrangement. Statement 2 is incorrect: The 65th Amendment substantially amended Article 338; Article 338-A came with the 89th Amendment in 2003. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Court held the provision directory. Statement 4 is incorrect: It bifurcated the combined commission and added Article 338-A. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A civil servant has no remedy in a court if the government decides a disciplinary case without consulting the Union Public Service Commission.
Statement-II: The Supreme Court has held that the provision for consultation is directory and not mandatory.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Because consultation is directory, an irregularity or absence of consultation does not invalidate the decision.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Governor cannot remove a member of the State Public Service Commission whom he has appointed.
Statement-II: The Governor may suspend such a member while the Supreme Court inquires into an allegation of misbehaviour.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Both are correct, but suspension pending inquiry is a separate power; it does not explain why removal lies with the President.
w: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I; it is a separate point
Statement-II is correct
Statement-I is correct

questions.q:
Match the following provisions of Part XIV of the Constitution with their subject-matter.

List-I
A. Article 316
B. Article 317
C. Article 320
D. Article 323

List-II
1. Functions of Public Service Commissions
2. Appointment and term of office of members
3. Reports of Public Service Commissions
4. Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission
questions.e: Article 316 deals with appointment and term, 317 with removal and suspension, 320 with functions and 323 with reports.

C and D are interchanged.
A and C are interchanged.

concepts.name: SC commission, evolution and the Public Service Commission comparison
concepts.description: The bifurcation of the SC and ST commission, the UPSC-SPSC comparison table, the timeline of commissions, and the NCSC's composition, functions, reports and powers.
concepts.idea: The NCSC under Article 338 is a five-member constitutional commission with advisory and civil-court-like powers whose reports reach Parliament through the President.
concepts.rule: The 89th Amendment (2003) split the combined commission into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under Article 338-A, the separate bodies existing from 2004. The NCSC has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three Members appointed by warrant, serving three years for at most two terms under the 2004 Rules. It investigates and monitors safeguards, inquires into complaints, advises on planning, recommends measures and reports to the President, who lays the reports before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum; State reports go through the Governor. It regulates its procedure, has the powers of a civil court, and must be consulted on major policy matters. The UPSC and SPSC differ in the appointing authority and age limit.
concepts.example: The NCSC can summon a person from any part of India but cannot punish for contempt.

questions.q: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two bodies. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes now function respectively under
questions.e: Article 338 now covers the NCSC and the new Article 338-A, inserted by the 89th Amendment, covers the NCST; the separate Commissions came into existence in 2004.
w: The Articles are reversed: the SC Commission stays under Article 338.
Article 338-B was added later, in 2018, for the Backward Classes Commission.
Article 338-B belongs to the National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.q: Which one of the following national commissions is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament and not a constitutional body?
questions.e: Contrasts the NCSC (Article 338) with the National Commission for Women (1992), Minorities (1993), the NHRC (1993) and the Commission for Protection of Child Rights (2007), which are statutory; the NCBC became constitutional in 2018.
w: It is directly established by Article 338.
It is directly established by Article 338-A.
It became a constitutional body under Article 338-B by the 102nd Amendment of 2018.

questions.q: The members of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes hold office for
questions.a: three years under the Rules made by the President, and cannot be appointed for more than two terms
o: three years under the Rules made by the President, and cannot be appointed for more than two terms
five years under the Rules made by the President, with eligibility for reappointment
six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, without reappointment
three years under the Rules made by the President, and may be reappointed any number of times
questions.e: The NCSC Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members hold office for three years under the 2004 Rules and not for more than two terms.
w: The term is three years, not five.
Six years and age 65 are the UPSC and the Election Commission terms.
A member cannot be appointed for more than two terms.

questions.q: A report of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes that pertains to a State Government is forwarded by the President to
questions.a: the Governor, who places it before the State Legislature with a memorandum on action taken and reasons for non-acceptance
o: the Governor, who places it before the State Legislature with a memorandum on action taken and reasons for non-acceptance
the Chief Minister, who places it before the State Legislature with a note on the action taken on its recommendations
the State Legislature directly, with a memorandum from the Commission on the action taken by the State
the State Commission for Scheduled Castes, which lays it before the State Legislature each year
questions.e: Reports go to the President, who lays them before Parliament; a report on a State goes to the Governor, who lays it before the State Legislature with the memorandum. Contrast the NCBC, whose State reports go to the State government.
w: The Governor, not the Chief Minister, is the channel for this Commission.
The President does not send it directly to the Legislature.
The Governor places it, not a State Commission.

questions.q: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1990 provided for a multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs. That constitutional commission replaced
questions.a: the Commissioner for SCs and STs as well as the Commission set up under the Resolution of 1987
o: the Commissioner for SCs and STs as well as the Commission set up under the Resolution of 1987
the Commissioner for SCs and STs as well as the National Commission for Backward Classes
the Commission set up in 1978 and the National Commission for Minorities
the Special Officer for linguistic minorities and the Commission set up under the Resolution of 1987
questions.e: The 65th Amendment (1990) turned the arrangement into a constitutional commission under Article 338, replacing the Commissioner and the Commission of the 1987 Resolution.
w: The NCBC was set up only in 1993.
The National Commission for Minorities was a different body, created in 1993.
The Special Officer for linguistic minorities is unrelated to SCs and STs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of commissions for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:

1. In 1950 the original Constitution provided for a Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
2. In 1978 a non-statutory multi-member Commission for SCs and STs was set up by a government resolution.
3. In 1987 a government resolution converted the combined Commission into a constitutional body.
4. In 1993 the National Commission for Backward Classes was constituted as a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 338 originally provided this. Statement 2 is correct: The Commissioner's office also continued. Statement 3 is incorrect: The 1987 resolution only modified its functions and renamed it the National Commission for SCs and STs; it remained non-constitutional. Statement 4 is correct: It became constitutional only in 2018.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional amendments relating to these commissions:

1. The 65th Amendment of 1990 made the multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs a constitutional body under Article 338.
2. The 89th Amendment of 2003 split the combined Commission into the NCSC under Article 338-A and the NCST under Article 338.
3. The 102nd Amendment of 2018 placed the Backward Classes Commission on a constitutional footing through Article 338-B.
4. After the 89th Amendment, the separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes was formally established in 2004.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It replaced the single Special Officer. Statement 2 is incorrect: The NCSC is under Article 338 and the NCST under Article 338-A. Statement 3 is correct: The Backward Classes Commission was placed on par with the other two. Statement 4 is correct: It came into existence in 2004.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the Union Public Service Commission and the State Public Service Commissions:

1. The Constitution does not fix the strength of either; it is left to the President for the UPSC and to the Governor for a State Commission.
2. The members of both the UPSC and the State Commissions are appointed by the President, the Governor merely forwarding names for the State Commissions.
3. UPSC members hold office for six years or till 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, while State Commission members do so for six years or till 62 years of age.
4. No qualification is prescribed except that one-third of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Strength is discretionary. Statement 2 is incorrect: UPSC members are appointed by the President and State Commission members by the Governor. Statement 3 is correct: The age limits differ. Statement 4 is incorrect: The proportion is one-half.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Public Service Commissions:

1. In the case of both the UPSC and a State Commission, a member can be removed for misbehaviour by the Governor after an inquiry by the High Court.
2. The salaries of the UPSC are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, and those of a State Commission on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
3. The Commissions conduct examinations, for All India and Central services in the case of the UPSC and for State services in the case of a State Commission, and advise on recruitment rules and disciplinary matters.
4. A Joint State Public Service Commission serving two or more States is created by the State Legislatures concerned by a joint law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: In both cases the President removes after a Supreme Court inquiry under Article 317. Statement 2 is correct: Charged expenses are not voted. Statement 3 is correct: Their roles run in parallel. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is created by Parliament on the request of the State Legislatures concerned.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

1. It investigates and monitors the constitutional and other legal safeguards for Scheduled Castes and evaluates their working.
2. It inquires into specific complaints of deprivation of rights and denial of safeguards, such as those on employment, education and reservation.
3. It participates in the planning of the socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes but has no role in evaluating their progress.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reports of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes:

1. Its annual report is submitted to the Prime Minister, who has it laid before Parliament.
2. The President has its reports laid before both Houses of Parliament with a memorandum on the action taken and the reasons for rejecting any recommendation.
3. A report concerning a State Government goes to the Chief Minister, who places it before the State Legislature.
4. Its recommendations are not binding and carry persuasive and moral authority.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The annual report goes to the President. Statement 2 is correct: The memorandum is part of the process. Statement 3 is incorrect: the President forwards it to the State Governor, who places it before the State Legislature; it does not go to the Chief Minister (Article 338 itself speaks of the State Government, not the Chief Minister). Statement 4 is correct: It is recommendatory.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:

3. It can require the discovery and production of documents, receive evidence on affidavits, requisition a public record from any court or office, and issue summons for witnesses.
4. It can punish a person for contempt of the Commission as a High Court does.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The residual clause and procedural freedom exist. Statement 2 is correct: Civil-court powers are conferred. Statement 3 is correct: These are the listed matters. Statement 4 is incorrect: Its powers are those of a civil court trying a suit; it is not a court of record.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

2. Article 338(10) provides that references to Scheduled Castes include references to the Anglo-Indian community, so the Commission discharges similar functions for that community.
3. Until 2018 the Commission also discharged similar functions for the other backward classes, and it was relieved of them by the 102nd Amendment Act.
4. The National Commission for Women, the National Commission for Minorities and the National Human Rights Commission are statutory bodies established by Acts of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The duty relates to all major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes. Statement 2 is correct: It reports to the President on safeguards for the community. Statement 3 is correct: The NCBC took over. Statement 4 is correct: Unlike the NCSC they are not created by the Constitution.

3. The National Commission for Backward Classes was constituted in 1993 under a provision of the Constitution.

3. It has a Chairperson and a Vice-Chairperson along with four more Members.
4. It can call for a public record from any court or office.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the work of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes:

2. It cannot summon a person who lives outside the State in which it sits.
3. It also discharges any other function relating to the protection and welfare of Scheduled Castes that the President may specify.
4. The duty to consult it on major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes binds the Central Government but not the State Governments.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is a listed function. Statement 2 is incorrect: It can summon a person from any part of India. Statement 3 is correct: The residual function clause. Statement 4 is incorrect: It binds both. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The recommendations of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes are not binding and carry persuasive and moral authority.
Statement-II: While investigating a complaint, the Commission has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit, including summoning any person and examining him on oath.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I

But these powers help the Commission collect evidence; they say nothing about whether its recommendations bind, so II does not explain I.
w: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I: civil-court powers concern gathering evidence, not whether the recommendations bind.

Consider the following statements:

Statement-II: These powers make the Commission a court of law that can punish offenders and issue binding orders.

Statement-I is correct

concepts.name: ST and Backward Classes commissions: composition, functions, powers and reports
concepts.description: The NCST's composition, functions, 2005 additional functions, powers and reports, and the NCBC's composition, functions and constitutional status.
concepts.idea: The NCST and NCBC mirror the NCSC in structure but differ in articles, rules and the channel for State reports.
concepts.rule: The NCST (Article 338-A, from 2004) and NCBC (Article 338-B, from 2018) each have a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three Members appointed by warrant for three years with at most two terms. The NCST's functions mirror the NCSC's and the 2005 Rules add minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, livelihood, displacement, land alienation, forest protection, PESA and shifting cultivation. The NCBC, set up in 1993 after Indra Sawhney, became constitutional through the 102nd Amendment, which also inserted Article 342-A; the 1993 Act was repealed in 2018 and its Rules date from 2018. NCST reports on a State go through the Governor, NCBC reports to the State government.
concepts.example: An NCBC report on a State is sent to the State government and not to the Governor.

questions.q: One reason for setting up a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was the creation in 1999 of a new Ministry whose task was to coordinate all activities relating to the Scheduled Tribes. That Ministry is the Ministry of
questions.e: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was created in 1999 for sharper focus on tribal welfare, and it was not administratively feasible for the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to coordinate it; the 89th Amendment then created a separate Commission formally established in 2004.
w: That Ministry continues to coordinate the activities relating to Scheduled Castes.
Minority Affairs deals with minorities, not tribal welfare.
Rural Development was not the Ministry created for this purpose.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and the National Commission for Backward Classes have which one of the following features in common?
questions.a: A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members, each holding office for three years under Rules made by the President
o: A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members, each holding office for three years under Rules made by the President
A Chairperson and four other Members, each holding office for three years under Rules made by the President for the purpose
A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members, each holding office for five years under an Act of Parliament passed for the purpose
A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other Members, each holding office for six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
questions.e: Each has one Chairperson, one Vice-Chairperson and three other Members appointed by the President by warrant, with three-year terms and a limit of two terms under Rules made by the President.
w: Each has a Vice-Chairperson as well, with three other Members.
The term is three years and the Rules are made by the President, not an Act.
Six years or age 65 is the term of the UPSC and the Election Commission, not of these Commissions.

questions.q: Among the additional functions specified for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes by the President in 2005 is the taking of measures to reduce and ultimately eliminate the practice of
questions.a: shifting cultivation by tribals that leads to their continuous disempowerment and degradation of land

grazing of cattle in the notified forest areas by tribal communities living in or near the forest reserves of the State
the collection of minor forest produce by tribals living in the forest areas for their own domestic livelihood
the use of tribal languages as the medium of instruction in the primary schools of the Scheduled Areas
questions.e: The 2005 Specification of Other Functions Rules include shifting cultivation, minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, livelihood, displacement, land alienation, forest protection and PESA.

The list says nothing on tribal languages.

questions.a: the State Government (and not to the Governor), which places it before the State Legislature with a memorandum on action taken
o: the State Government (and not to the Governor), which places it before the State Legislature with a memorandum on action taken
the Governor, who places it before the State Legislature with a memorandum on the action taken on its recommendations
the State Legislature directly, with a memorandum on action taken from the Commission
the State Backward Classes Commission, which places it before the State Legislature
questions.e: And fn.6: under clause 7 of Article 338B the President forwards the NCBC's State report to the State government and not to the Governor; the NCST and NCSC route it through the Governor.

questions.q: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Article 338-B and also inserted Article 342-A. Article 342-A
questions.a: enables the President to specify the socially and educationally backward classes
o: enables the President to specify the socially and educationally backward classes
enables the Governor of a State, by public notification, to specify the socially and educationally backward classes

empowers the National Commission for Backward Classes to notify the list of backward classes

Specification of Scheduled Tribes is under Article 342, not 342-A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition and tenure of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:

1. The separate Commission was formally established in 2004, after the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
2. It is a multi-member constitutional body with one Chairperson, one Vice-Chairperson and three other Members.

4. One of them is to improve the relief and rehabilitation measures for tribal groups displaced by development projects.

Consider the following statements about the 2005 functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:

1. It includes recommending viable livelihood strategies focused on skill development and forest and non-forest livelihoods, and measures to prevent alienation of tribal land and to rehabilitate those already alienated.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes:

1. The separate Commission was formally established in 2004.
2. Its Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members hold office for four years from the date of assuming office.
3. A report of the Commission about a State is laid directly before the State Legislature by the Chairperson of the Commission.
4. No member can be appointed for more than three terms.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It came into being after the 89th Amendment. Statement 2 is incorrect: The term is three years. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Chairperson does not lay it; a State report is forwarded to the Governor or the State Government (Art. 338-A), which lays it. Statement 4 is incorrect: The limit is two terms. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Backward Classes:

1. It presents annual reports, and special reports when needed, to the President on the working of the safeguards.
2. It participates in and advises on the planning for the socio-economic development of backward classes and evaluates progress under Union and State schemes.
3. Complaints before it often involve improper denial of reservation, exclusion from OBC lists and administrative arbitrariness.
4. It is a statutory body functioning under the NCBC Act, 1993.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is a listed function. Statement 2 is correct: Planning and evaluation are listed. Statement 3 is correct: These are typical complaints. Statement 4 is incorrect: It is a constitutional body under Article 338-B. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional commissions for the weaker sections:

1. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under Article 338, with a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three Members appointed by the President by warrant.
2. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is a constitutional body under Article 338-A, created by the 89th Amendment (2003).
3. The National Commission for Backward Classes functions under Article 338-A.
4. The 65th Amendment Act of 1990 created a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The terms and conditions are set by the President through rules. Statement 2 is correct: It was created by bifurcation. Statement 3 is incorrect: It functions under Article 338-B. Statement 4 is incorrect: the 65th Amendment (1990) set up the combined SC and ST commission; the separate ST Commission came with the 89th Amendment (2003). So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I

So II explains I.
w: Statement-II does explain Statement-I: the new ministry is why a separate commission was needed.
